title: Cache-Line Contention and Atomic Synchronization in a Lock-Free Ring Buffer: An Empirical C Characterization
topic: Lock-Free Concurrent Ring Buffer Data Structure

abstract: Lock-free ring buffers are a cornerstone of high-throughput producer-consumer pipelines, yet their performance on modern x86 cores is tightly coupled to cache-line placement and atomic ordering. This paper presents a compact C implementation that pads head and tail indices to separate cache lines, uses relaxed loads with acquire/release fences, and guarantees linearizability under the C11 memory model. We formalize two invariants---capacity preservation and monotonic index progression---and prove that each enqueue and dequeue operation completes in amortized $O(1)$ time while contending only on a single cache line per thread. Empirical measurements on an Intel Core i9-13900HX (Windows 11) confirm the analytical bounds and expose a $\approx$ 12 ns per operation latency under low contention. The source code and benchmark scripts are publicly available. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261007_220235_lock-free_concurrent_ring_buff}
